explanation:
I found no single Mathlib declaration that states this bound, `p ≤ |N(x)|` for nonzero `x` in an ideal `P` lying over `(p)`.

The nearest declarations are `Ideal.absNorm_dvd_norm_of_mem` (in `RingTheory/Ideal/Norm/AbsNorm.lean`), `Ideal.absNorm_dvd_absNorm_of_le` and `Int.absNorm_under_dvd_absNorm`. These only give divisibility, `absNorm I ∣ Algebra.norm ℤ x` for `x ∈ I`. A derivation from them has to prove that `p` divides `absNorm P` from the `under` hypothesis. It then needs positivity of the norm for nonzero `x` and `Nat.le_of_dvd`. The library's own proof already does this in several steps, through its helper lemmas `prime_dvd_integerNorm_of_mem_idealAbove` and `integerNorm_natAbs_pos`.

I grepped `NumberField` and `Ideal/Norm` for `natAbs`/`absNorm` lemmas of the form `≤`. I also looked at the one `NumberField/Ideal/Basic.lean` use of `absNorm_dvd_norm_of_mem`. None of them states the `≤` form with `P.under ℤ = span {p}`.
